title: Naturality and shifts of the tensor mate of an arbitrary arrow
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories, with bifunctors $\otimes_{\mathcal C}:\mathcal C\times\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $\otimes_{\mathcal D}:\mathcal D\times\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$, both denoted $\otimes$. Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ have a specified adjunction $L\dashv R$ with natural unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RL$ and counit $\varepsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}$ satisfying the triangle identities [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Fix a natural isomorphism $\mu_{M,P}:L(M\otimes P)\xrightarrow{\sim}LM\otimes LP$. For each $K\in\mathcal C$, $E\in\mathcal D$, and morphism $c:LK\to E$, put
$$F_K(P)=K\otimes P,\quad H_E(P)=E\otimes LP,\quad G_E=RH_E,\quad \beta^c_P=(c\otimes1_{LP})\mu_{K,P},\quad \alpha^c_P=R(\beta^c_P)\eta_{K\otimes P}.$$
Suppose the categories have coherent shifts $[n]$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, each an auto-equivalence, and $L,R$ and every functor $T_M=M\otimes-$ have coherent natural shift comparisons, as in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Write $l,r,t^M$ for these comparisons. Require the tensor comparisons to be natural in the fixed input $M$, require $\eta$ to commute with every shift for the induced comparison of $RL$, and require $\mu_{K,-}:LF_K\to T_{LK}L$ to commute with the composite comparisons for every $K,n$. In detail put
$$a_{n,P}=l_{n,F_KP}L(t^K_{n,P}),\quad b_{n,P}=t^{LK}_{n,LP}T_{LK}(l_{n,P}),\quad h_{n,P}=t^E_{n,LP}T_E(l_{n,P}),\quad g_{n,P}=r_{n,H_EP}R(h_{n,P}),$$
and assume $b_{n,P}\mu_{K,P[n]}=\mu_{K,P}[n]a_{n,P}$ and $r_{n,LX}R(l_{n,X})\eta_{X[n]}=\eta_X[n]$.
Then for all $K,E,c,P,n$,
$$h_{n,P}\beta^c_{P[n]}=\beta^c_P[n]a_{n,P},\qquad g_{n,P}\alpha^c_{P[n]}=\alpha^c_P[n]t^K_{n,P}.$$
Moreover, for $K'\in\mathcal C$, $E'\in\mathcal D$, $c':LK'\to E'$, $a:K\to K'$, $b:E\to E'$ with $bc=c'L(a)$, and every $p:P\to P'$, one has
$$(b\otimes Lp)\beta^c_P=\beta^{c'}_{P'}L(a\otimes p),\qquad R(b\otimes Lp)\alpha^c_P=\alpha^{c'}_{P'}(a\otimes p).$$
No exactness, tensor associator, unit object, or invertibility of $c$ or $\alpha^c$ is required.

proof.text: Write composition in functional order, with the rightmost map applied first. For $Q\in\mathcal D$ put $\theta_Q=c\otimes1_Q:LK\otimes Q\to E\otimes Q$. Bifunctoriality gives $(1_E\otimes q)\theta_Q=\theta_{Q'}(1_{LK}\otimes q)$ for $q:Q\to Q'$, since both sides equal $c\otimes q$. The adjunction formula $\Psi(u)=R(u)\eta$ identifies $\alpha^c_P$ with the adjunct of $\beta^c_P=\theta_{LP}\mu_{K,P}$. Thus these formulas use the specified adjunction, rather than a separate choice of mate.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
For $a,b,p,c,c'$ as in the statement, bifunctoriality, $bc=c'L(a)$, and naturality of $\mu$ give
$$\begin{aligned}(b\otimes Lp)\beta^c_P&=(bc\otimes Lp)\mu_{K,P}\\&=(c'\otimes1_{LP'})(L(a)\otimes Lp)\mu_{K,P}\\&=(c'\otimes1_{LP'})\mu_{K',P'}L(a\otimes p)=\beta^{c'}_{P'}L(a\otimes p).\end{aligned}$$
In particular $a=1_K,b=1_E,c'=c$ proves naturality of $\beta^c$ in $P$. This calculation uses only the naturality and bifunctor axioms specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
Put $u=a\otimes p$ and $v=b\otimes Lp$. Naturality of the adjunction unit is $RL(u)\eta_{K\otimes P}=\eta_{K'\otimes P'}u$. Applying $R$ to the preceding step therefore gives
$$R(v)\alpha^c_P=R(v\beta^c_P)\eta_{K\otimes P}=R(\beta^{c'}_{P'})RL(u)\eta_{K\otimes P}=\alpha^{c'}_{P'}u.$$
Taking $a,b$ to be identities gives naturality of $\alpha^c$ in $P$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
Fix any integer $n$. Naturality in the fixed tensor input, which is an explicit hypothesis on $t$, gives
$$t^E_{n,Q}\theta_{Q[n]}=\theta_Q[n]t^{LK}_{n,Q}.$$
Apply step 1 to $q=l_{n,P}:L(P[n])\to(LP)[n]$, and then this identity to $Q=LP$. By the definitions of $h$ and $b_{n,P}$ the result is
$$h_{n,P}\theta_{L(P[n])}=t^E_{n,LP}T_E(l_{n,P})\theta_{L(P[n])}=\theta_{LP}[n]t^{LK}_{n,LP}T_{LK}(l_{n,P})=\theta_{LP}[n]b_{n,P}.$$
Here the composite comparisons are precisely those in the cited shift-compatibility convention, applied at the fixed shift $n$.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
Now compose the identity of step 4 with $\mu_{K,P[n]}$ and use the assumed compatibility of $\mu$:
$$h_{n,P}\beta^c_{P[n]}=\theta_{LP}[n]b_{n,P}\mu_{K,P[n]}=\theta_{LP}[n]\mu_{K,P}[n]a_{n,P}=\beta^c_P[n]a_{n,P}.$$
The last equality is preservation of composition by $[n]$. This proves the first shift equation for every $n$, without making any assertion that the single arrow $c$ itself has a shift comparison.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
For the second shift equation set $X=K\otimes P$, $X'=K\otimes P[n]$, and $s=t^K_{n,P}:X'\to X[n]$. Then $a_{n,P}=l_{n,X}L(s)$. Unit naturality at $s$, followed by the assumed shift equation for $\eta$ at $X$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}r_{n,LX}R(a_{n,P})\eta_{X'}&=r_{n,LX}R(l_{n,X})RL(s)\eta_{X'}\\&=r_{n,LX}R(l_{n,X})\eta_{X[n]}s=\eta_X[n]s.\end{aligned}$$
All maps in this equality go from $X'$ to $(RLX)[n]$. In particular no compatibility with a tensor shift in the first variable is used.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), agent-written arbitrary-arrow expansion; shift and naturality calculations below are not asserted by the tag.

proof.text:
Naturality of $r_n$ at $\beta^c_P:LX\to H_EP$ reads
$$r_{n,H_EP}R(\beta^c_P[n])=R(\beta^c_P)[n]r_{n,LX}.$$
Using step 5, this equality, and step 6, expand the left-hand side of the desired equation:
$$\begin{aligned}g_{n,P}\alpha^c_{P[n]}&=r_{n,H_EP}R(h_{n,P}\beta^c_{P[n]})\eta_{X'}\\&=r_{n,H_EP}R(\beta^c_P[n])R(a_{n,P})\eta_{X'}\\&=R(\beta^c_P)[n]\eta_X[n]s=\alpha^c_P[n]t^K_{n,P}.\end{aligned}$$
The last equality again uses functoriality of $[n]$. Together with steps 2, 3 and 5 this proves every displayed conclusion. Only functoriality, naturality and the stated compatibility equations were used.
